Salesforce is no longer just selling AI agents. It is building the operating architecture to run them at enterprise scale.

Ahead of Dreamforce 2026, the company announced job-ready Agentforce agents alongside two critical new layers: an Enterprise AI Harness and an AI Control Plane. The Control Plane is the standout — a centralized governance system for managing agent behavior, data access, and policy enforcement across the entire organization.

This matters because the biggest challenge in enterprise AI right now is not getting one agent to work. It is getting dozens of them to work together without creating ungoverned fragmentation across departments.

Salesforce is making a clear strategic bet: the most valuable position in enterprise AI is not the model layer. It is the orchestration and governance layer that sits above it. The company that controls how agents are deployed, monitored, and constrained captures the stickiest enterprise relationship.

For every CTO evaluating their AI stack — the question is no longer whether you have AI agents. It is whether your architecture can govern and orchestrate them at scale.
